questions.q: Both backs are pressed. Where should our keeper move to become the third builder?
options: Up behind the backs, in the middle
Into midfield beside the central midfielder
questions.explain: Right. From the middle the keeper can reach both backs, and all three midfielders stay ahead.
choiceExplanations: That crowds the ball. The keeper can no longer offer a pass to the other back.
Right. From the middle the keeper can reach both backs, and all three midfielders stay ahead.
Now nobody supports behind the backs, and the keeper leaves the goal wide open.

questions.q: True or false? Here our central midfielder should drop to help the right back.
questions.explain: Right, it's false. The right midfielder already helps outside, so the central midfielder keeps the middle link.
choiceExplanations: The right midfielder already gives that outside pass. Dropping the central midfielder empties the middle.
Right, it's false. The right midfielder already helps outside, so the central midfielder keeps the middle link.

questions.q: Now the left back has it. Blue screens the keeper and centre. Which pass helps?
questions.explain: Yes. The left midfielder comes down the outside, so the central midfielder can stay in the middle.
choiceExplanations: Blue's striker stands in that lane, so the return to the keeper is blocked.
A Blue midfielder screens that lane, so the pass would be cut out.
Yes. The left midfielder comes down the outside, so the central midfielder can stay in the middle.
